documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Winter follow-up. Mood flat this winter, PHQ-9 11, item 9 zero. Therapy has drifted to monthly. Sertraline daily.

Night meds (phenytoin, desmopressin, now Biktarvy too) are going well with the roommate's help. Morning desmopressin and folic acid sometimes forgotten. She has not been back to ID since September — says she keeps meaning to call. No seizures. Drove for the first time last month after the waiting period.

O: vitals as charted. Alert, a little subdued. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. HIV — overdue with ID and last VL was detectable. Our MA called ID with her in the room and booked her for March. Reinforced daily Biktarvy.
2. MDD, recurrent — mild-moderate; continue sertraline 100; encouraged weekly therapy again.
3. Epilepsy — phenytoin level and BMP today.
4. Central DI — stable.
RTC 4–6 months.

reports.text: Indication: headache, confusion, advanced HIV. Technique: noncontrast axial CT head. Findings: Four hypodense lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter. No acute hemorrhage. No hydrocephalus. No midline shift. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Four hypodense lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter; MRI with contrast recommended.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. Findings: Four ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter. No hydrocephalus. No midline shift. No extra-axial collection. Normal flow voids.
reports.conclusion: Four ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter; in the setting of advanced HIV, toxoplasmosis is favored.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (2024-05-22)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — 05/22/2024 16:30

33-year-old woman with advanced HIV, generalized epilepsy and central DI, brought by her roommate for several days of headache and confusion. Headache is dull, at the back of the head, worsening each day. Roommate says she cannot keep her attention on anything and has been more and more sleepy. Per the roommate and records, she has been taking her HIV medicine poorly.

Allergies: SULFONAMIDES — anaphylaxis; latex.
Meds per list: phenytoin, desmopressin, Biktarvy, sertraline, folic acid, prenatal vitamin.

Afebrile. BP 110/65, HR 94, RR 16.
Exam: oriented to self only. No papilledema on fundoscopy. No meningismus. Moves all extremities.

CD4 50. Noncontrast CT: four hypodense lesions basal ganglia/subcortical white matter → MRI with contrast obtained next morning (ring-enhancing, see report).

Impression: CNS lesions in advanced HIV, toxoplasmosis most likely. Admit medicine, ID consult. Sulfa anaphylaxis noted — no sulfadiazine.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (05/22–06/03/2024)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/22/2024 — discharged 06/03/2024. Medicine service with infectious disease consultation.

Principal diagnosis: cerebral toxoplasmosis.
Other: HIV, CDC stage 3, CD4 50, HIV RNA 214,000 copies/mL (nonadherence); generalized epilepsy; central DI; recurrent major depression.

Course: Toxoplasma IgG positive. MRI brain: four ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter. Because of her sulfonamide anaphylaxis, treated with pyrimethamine (200 mg load, then 50 mg daily), clindamycin 600 mg every 6 hours and leucovorin 10 mg daily, planned for 6 weeks. Atovaquone 1500 mg daily started for Pneumocystis prophylaxis. Biktarvy restarted on hospital day 10 per ID, with adherence planning. Headache resolved and attention improved day by day; no seizures. Phenytoin, desmopressin, sertraline continued; sodium normal throughout. At discharge oriented to person, place and time, walking independently.

Discharge medications:
- pyrimethamine 25 mg tabs: 50 mg daily
- clindamycin 300 mg caps: 600 mg every 6 hours
- leucovorin 5 mg tabs: 10 mg daily
- atovaquone 750 mg/5 mL: 10 mL daily with food
- Biktarvy 1 tab daily (bedtime)
- phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS; desmopressin 0.1 mg BID; sertraline 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (CBC weekly while on pyrimethamine); ID clinic in 4–6 weeks with repeat MRI. Pharmacy alerted: pyrimethamine requires prior authorization.

Hospitalist

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called 2 days after discharge. Pt home; roommate with her. Headache gone. Thinking clearer, "still a little foggy." Has clindamycin, leucovorin, atovaquone and her usual meds. Pharmacy did NOT fill pyrimethamine — needs prior auth; hospital gave a 3-day supply. Started PA today (urgent). Visit 6/11. Reviewed: call or ED for worse headache, confusion, seizure, rash, fever.

documents.title: Prior Authorization — pyrimethamine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Medicaid prior authorization for pyrimethamine 25 mg tabs submitted 6/5 with discharge summary and ID note; APPROVED 6/6 through 12/2024. Pharmacy filled same day; pt picked up — no missed doses per pt. Renewal reminder set.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit.

Admitted 5/22–6/3 with headache and confusion: cerebral toxoplasmosis (4 ring-enhancing lesions, basal ganglia/subcortical white matter), CD4 50, VL 214,000. On pyrimethamine/clindamycin/leucovorin (no sulfadiazine — anaphylaxis), atovaquone for PJP prophylaxis, Biktarvy restarted.

Today with roommate. Headache gone. Says her head is "90% clear." No seizures, no fever, no rash, no diarrhea on clindamycin. Pyrimethamine PA approved, has it. Taking every dose — the roommate built a chart on the fridge. Lost weight in the hospital.

Mood: scared, ashamed about letting the HIV meds slide. PHQ-9 12; denies SI. Wants to restart therapy.

Exam: vitals as charted; weight 57 kg. Alert, oriented x3, recalls 3/3 at 5 minutes. Fundi without papilledema. CN intact. Strength 5/5, sensation intact, gait normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Skin no rash.

A/P:
1. Cerebral toxoplasmosis — improving clinically. Continue 6-week regimen; ID visit with repeat MRI early July. CBC/CMP today; CBC every 2 weeks during the acute course, then monthly for a few months (standing order).
2. HIV, advanced — Biktarvy daily at bedtime, supervised. ID following.
3. PJP prophylaxis — atovaquone.
4. MDD, recurrent — moderate; continue sertraline 100; message sent to her therapist to resume weekly.
5. Epilepsy, DI — stable; continue.
6. Weight — nutrition, recheck at next visit.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood counts are holding up well on the pyrimethamine and your kidney and liver tests are normal. Next blood count in 2 weeks — the standing order is in.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up (seen 2024-07-09)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, 07/09/2024

Cerebral toxoplasmosis, six weeks of pyrimethamine/clindamycin/leucovorin completed this week. Clinically well — no headache, sharp, back to some freelance work. Taking all doses (roommate supervised).

MRI 7/2: four lesions smaller with less enhancement. No new lesions.
Labs: CD4 88 cells/uL; HIV RNA 640 copies/mL (from 214,000). CBCs through PCP normal.

Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis); latex.

Plan:
- Step down to maintenance: pyrimethamine 25 mg daily, clindamycin 600 mg every 8 hours, leucovorin 10 mg daily. Continue until CD4 >200 for more than 6 months on suppressive ART.
- Atovaquone 1500 mg daily for PJP prophylaxis until CD4 >200 for 3 months.
- Biktarvy daily — great response so far.
- CBC monthly for the next few months, then every 3 months while on pyrimethamine (PCP); our labs every 3–4 months.

ID attending

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC normal on maintenance pyrimethamine/leucovorin. Continue monthly through October, then every 3 months. MA to notify pt via portal.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up (seen 2024-09-17)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology — 09/17/2024

Generalized epilepsy. Last seizure May 2023 (medication stop). Interval cerebral toxoplasmosis this spring with four ring-enhancing lesions, improving on MRI in July; no seizures during or since. Phenytoin ER 300 mg qHS, taken supervised.

Exam: normal neurological examination.
Allergies: sulfonamides, latex.

Plan: continue phenytoin. Lesions raise seizure risk — reviewed precautions again. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Inactivated flu (trivalent) L deltoid; 2024–25 COVID R deltoid. No live vaccines (CD4 low). Monthly CBC drawn at the same visit per standing order. Tolerated well.

documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, 11/12/2024

HIV RNA now undetectable. CD4 148 cells/uL (from 88). Doing well on toxoplasma maintenance (pyrimethamine 25 mg daily, clindamycin 600 mg q8h, leucovorin 10 mg daily) and atovaquone; no diarrhea, no rash. Adherence excellent.

Allergies: sulfonamides — anaphylaxis; latex.

Plan: continue all. Next labs and visit in about 6 months. PA for pyrimethamine due for renewal in December — our office will support.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. CD4 228 in May, VL undetectable. No seizures. DI controlled. Mood good; PHQ-9 8. Therapy wrapped up in the spring by mutual agreement. Taking sertraline.

Meds: phenytoin ER 300 qHS; desmopressin 0.1 BID; Biktarvy daily; sertraline 100; pyrimethamine 25 daily; clindamycin 600 q8h; leucovorin 10 daily; atovaquone 1500 daily; folic acid 1 mg; prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfonamides (anaphylaxis), latex.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 61.5 kg. Gen well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Breasts normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Ext no edema. Neuro nonfocal. Skin normal.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV co-test due fall 2026. Vaccines up to date; flu/COVID in fall.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids.
- HIV, toxo maintenance — per ID.
- MDD — in good place; continue sertraline.
- Epilepsy, DI — stable.
RTC 6 months.
